requirements.statement: The platform shall allow XATA employees to create, manage, prioritize, track and complete personal and team TODO items.
The platform shall provide a single centralized web application as a common place to manage TODO items, providing a single system for managing TODO items.
The platform shall allow users to quickly create and update TODO items (business objective; 'quickly' is not quantified in the source).
The platform shall provide visibility of open, completed and overdue work.
The platform shall allow team members to assign TODO items to one another.
The platform shall provide basic priority and due-date management for TODO items.
The platform shall provide a simple dashboard for work tracking.
The first release shall be intentionally small and easy to use.
The platform shall reduce dependency on spreadsheets, email and chat for TODO tracking (business objective).
System shall allow an authenticated user to create a TODO. Priority: Must.
A TODO shall contain title, description, status, priority and due date. Priority: Must.
Users shall be able to edit TODOs they own or are authorized to manage. Priority: Must.
Users shall be able to mark TODOs as completed. Priority: Must.
Users shall be able to mark TODOs as completed. Priority: Must.
Users shall be able to assign a TODO to another authorized user. Priority: Must.
System shall support Open, In Progress and Completed statuses. Priority: Must.
System shall support Low, Medium, High and Critical priorities. Priority: Must.
Users shall filter TODOs by status, priority, assignee and due date. Priority: Must.
Users shall search TODOs by title or description. Priority: Should.
Platform shall provide user login and a basic user profile.
Users shall be able to view and delete TODOs.
TODOs shall support optional notes in addition to description.
Platform shall provide a dashboard showing TODO status.
Platform shall provide a basic team view for assigned TODOs.
TODOs shall include audit information such as created date and updated date.
Employee role shall be able to create and manage own TODOs.
Employee role shall be able to view assigned TODOs and update their status.
Team Lead role shall be able to create and assign TODOs.
Team Lead role shall be able to view team TODOs and monitor overdue work.
Administrator role shall be able to manage users and basic platform configuration.
Dashboard shall show Open, In Progress, Completed and Overdue TODO counts. (Priority: Must)
Dashboard shall include High/Critical priority TODOs.
Team Leads shall view TODOs assigned to their team members. (Priority: Must)
System shall maintain created-by, created-date, updated-by and updated-date for each TODO. (Priority: Must)
Users shall be able to delete TODOs where permitted. (Priority: Should)
System shall prevent unauthorized modification of another user's TODO. (Priority: Must)
System shall provide a web interface through supported browsers. (Priority: Must)
Users shall be able to create a TODO by entering a title and description, selecting a priority and a due date, optionally assigning it to a user, and saving the TODO.
Users shall be able to view TODO details.
Users shall be able to edit TODO information.
Users shall be able to change TODO status.
Users shall be able to change TODO priority or due date.
Users shall be able to reassign TODOs where authorized.
A TODO must have a title.
A due date cannot be earlier than creation date unless explicitly permitted.
Completed TODOs must have Completed status.
Only authorized users can assign or modify TODOs. Users cannot modify TODOs outside their authorization.
Overdue means the due date has passed and the status is not Completed.
Deleting a TODO must not delete the user account or other TODOs.
Users can log in and create a TODO.
A TODO can be assigned, updated and completed.
Dashboard counts must correctly reflect TODO state.
Filtering and search must return correct results.
XATA can complete the core TODO lifecycle without administrator assistance.
Application meets agreed NFRs.
Initial release is web-based.
First release will use a single enterprise environment.
Normal page/API response time must be ≤ 2 seconds for 95% of requests under normal load.
TODO create/update operations must complete in ≤ 2 seconds for 95% of requests.
Dashboard loading must complete in ≤ 3 seconds for 95% of requests.
Search/filter response must be ≤ 2 seconds for 95% of requests.
The platform must support at least 500 concurrent active users.
Monthly availability shall be ≥ 99.5%, excluding agreed maintenance windows.
Planned maintenance shall be communicated ≥ 24 hours in advance.
After an application failure, service shall be restored within 30 minutes.
The solution shall support growth in users and TODO volume without major redesign.
The solution shall support at least 100,000 TODO records initially.
Application services should be horizontally scalable where practical.
Database design shall support future growth beyond initial capacity.
All users shall be authenticated before accessing protected functionality.
Authorization shall be role-based.
Users shall only access TODO data permitted by their role.
Data shall be encrypted in transit using HTTPS/TLS.
Sensitive credentials shall not be hard-coded.
If passwords are locally managed, they shall use secure industry-standard hashing.
The application shall protect against common web vulnerabilities, including injection, broken access control and XSS.
Administrative actions should be auditable.
TODO records shall have unique identifiers.
Required fields shall be validated server-side.
Updates shall not silently overwrite conflicting data.
Created and updated timestamps shall be stored consistently.
Referential integrity shall be maintained between TODOs and users.
Deleted data handling shall follow XATA's retention policy.
Core create/update/complete flow should require minimal steps.
UI shall be responsive for standard desktop and tablet screens.
Validation errors shall be understandable.
Status, priority and overdue items shall be visually distinguishable.
Common actions shall be discoverable without technical knowledge.
Target WCAG 2.1 AA principles where practical.
Keyboard navigation should support core workflows.
Form controls should have meaningful labels.
Text should have sufficient contrast and readable sizing.
Solution shall use modular, maintainable code.
Business logic shall be separated from presentation and persistence.
APIs and major components shall be documented.
Automated unit tests shall cover critical business logic.
Configuration shall be externalized from source code.
Logging shall support troubleshooting without exposing sensitive information.
Application errors shall be logged with sufficient troubleshooting context.
Health checks shall be available.
Key metrics should include request failures and response latency.
Logs should include correlation/request identifiers where appropriate.
Operational alerts should be configurable for service failures.
Production data shall be backed up according to an agreed schedule.
Backups shall be protected from unauthorized access.
Solution shall support restoration after major failure.
Target Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is 15 minutes, unless XATA agrees otherwise.
Target Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is 30 minutes.
Solution shall support current versions of major enterprise browsers such as Chrome and Edge.
Solution should avoid browser-specific functionality unless approved.
APIs should use documented, versionable interfaces.
Solution shall collect only data required for TODO management.
Access to personal and team information shall follow XATA authorization rules.
Sensitive information shall not be written to application logs.
Data retention and deletion shall follow XATA policy.
Critical application and database components shall have documented recovery procedures.
Recovery procedures shall be tested periodically.
XBS shall document dependencies required to restore the service.
XBS shall demonstrate compliance with agreed NFRs through appropriate testing, evidence, configuration review and operational validation before production acceptance.
Security NFR category has priority Must.
Performance NFR category has priority Must.
Availability NFR category has priority Must.
Data Integrity NFR category has priority Must.
Backup & Recovery NFR category has priority Must.
Usability NFR category has priority Must.
Maintainability NFR category has priority Must.
Accessibility NFR category has priority Should.
Advanced observability NFR category has priority Should.

open_questions.question: How is 'overdue' defined, and is it determined solely by the due date being in the past relative to an open (not completed) TODO item?
What constitutes a 'team' and how does team membership affect visibility of, and assignment of, TODO items?
What is the scale of priority levels, and what does 'basic' due-date management include (for example, reminders or notifications)?
What is the measurable meaning of 'quickly' for creating and updating TODO items, and what response-time or usability target applies?
What content and features are expected in the 'simple dashboard' for work tracking, and what defines the boundary of the 'intentionally small' first release?
BR-003 and BR-005 rely on 'authorized to manage' and 'authorized user' without defining the authorization model or who qualifies (e.g., Team Lead scope, Employee rights).
Team Lead 'team' and 'team TODOs' are not defined; the membership basis for team view and team-level assignment is unspecified.
'Overdue work' is not defined, and no rule (e.g., due date passed while not Completed) is stated.
Notes are listed in scope as optional, but BR-002 does not include notes in the TODO content; it is unclear whether notes are a required field or a separate capability.
The scope of 'basic platform configuration' for the Administrator role and the meaning of 'basic user profile' are not defined.
The evidence contains no non-functional requirements (e.g., performance, availability, security, accessibility, audit retention); confirm whether NFR evidence exists beyond the supplied chunks.
What rules define authorization for reassigning and deleting TODOs? The BRD uses 'where authorized' in Section 7.2 and 'where permitted' in BR-013, and does not define who holds that authority.
Which priority values are available? Section 7.1 requires selecting a priority and Section 7.3 refers to High/Critical priority TODOs, but the BRD does not list the priority levels.

Which TODO status values are available for the Change status function? BR-010 names Open, In Progress, Completed and Overdue, but the BRD does not confirm whether Overdue is a status or a derived condition.
Which browsers are supported for the web interface? BR-015 refers to 'supported browsers' without naming them or specifying versions.

Does the dashboard display High/Critical priority TODOs as a count, and how is an Overdue TODO defined? Section 7.3 lists these items without defining their measures or the criteria for overdue status.
Who may explicitly permit a due date earlier than the creation date, and how is that permission recorded?
The acceptance criterion 'Application meets agreed NFRs' refers to NFRs that are not defined in the supplied evidence. Which NFRs are agreed, and what are their thresholds?
Which users are considered 'authorized' to assign or modify TODOs, and how is authorization defined and granted?
How is a TODO with no due date classified for overdue status, given that overdue requires a passed due date?
NFR-PERF-001 refers to 'normal load' but the evidence does not define normal load (for example, user count, request volume, or peak-versus-off-peak conditions).
The evidence does not state the load conditions, measurement window, or measurement method under which the 95% response-time targets (NFR-PERF-002, -003, -004) must be met.
NFR-PERF-005 does not define 'active user' or the time period over which concurrency is measured.
What constitutes an 'agreed maintenance window', who agrees it, and how is it documented?
How is monthly availability measured and calculated (measurement tool, period definition, and treatment of partial outages)?
What does 'without major redesign' mean in measurable terms, and what growth targets in users and TODO volume apply beyond the initial 100,000 records?
What is the 'where practical' condition for horizontal scalability, and which application services are in scope?
Will passwords be locally managed, or will an external identity provider be used? This determines whether the hashing requirement applies.
Which administrative actions must be auditable, how long audit records must be retained, and does 'should' indicate an optional or mandatory obligation?
How are conflicting updates detected and resolved (for example, versioning or optimistic locking), and what is the expected user behaviour on conflict?
What are the contents of XATA's retention policy, and what retention periods and deletion methods apply to deleted TODO and user data?
What does 'minimal steps' mean for the core create/update/complete flow? No step count or measurable threshold is given.
Which 'standard desktop and tablet screens' are in scope (screen sizes, resolutions, orientations, browsers)?
Which WCAG 2.1 AA principles or success criteria are in scope, and what makes conformance 'practical' versus excused?
What measurable thresholds define 'sufficient contrast' and 'readable sizing' for text?
Which components or logic constitute 'critical business logic', and what test coverage or pass criteria are expected?
What content defines 'sufficient troubleshooting context' for error logs, and in which cases are correlation/request identifiers 'appropriate'?
What is the agreed backup schedule for production data (frequency, retention, and who agrees it)?
How and by whom is XATA's agreement to a different RPO than 15 minutes given, and what alternative values are acceptable?
Is the browser list limited to Chrome and Edge, or are other major enterprise browsers required? Which versions count as current?
Who approves browser-specific functionality, and through what process?
What information is classified as sensitive for the logging restriction?
What are the XATA data retention and deletion policy periods and rules, and where is that policy available?
Which application and database components are classified as critical, and how often must recovery procedures be tested?
What does XBS refer to, and what is the required format or level of detail for the dependency documentation?
The NFR section refers to 'agreed NFRs' but the supplied evidence does not contain the NFR statements, thresholds, or measurement criteria for any category. What are the agreed NFR specifics?

The priority table uses 'Must' and 'Should' without defining their obligation strength or the consequence of not meeting a 'Should' priority. How should these priorities be interpreted for acceptance?
